title: PIM-STM: Software Transactional Memory for Processing-In-Memory Systems
problem: Processing-In-Memory systems lack efficient synchronization mechanisms for concurrent access, requiring expensive synchronization primitives that can offset the performance benefits of reduced data movement.
motivation: Efficient concurrency control in PIM systems is essential to achieve the full performance potential of in-memory processing for data-intensive applications.
method: The system adds Software Transactional Memory—a coordination mechanism for simultaneous operations—by running all transaction management (tracking which operations access what data) inside the Processing-In-Memory chip itself, avoiding expensive messages to the host computer. It uses optimistic concurrency control, letting transactions run simultaneously without locks (access restrictions), then checking for conflicts; if conflicts occurred, the system rolls back and retries the affected transaction.
key_novelty: This work implements Software Transactional Memory (a system for coordinating multiple simultaneous operations) directly on Processing-In-Memory chips, allowing concurrent access without the expensive synchronization overhead that normally limits these systems.
contributions: STM design adapted to PIM hardware capabilities and architectural constraints
Efficient transaction management and conflict detection mechanisms for PIM
Reduced synchronization overhead between CPU and PIM units
Performance improvements for concurrent workloads on PIM systems
